review.tagline: Bash loop that reruns Amp or Claude Code until every PRD story passes
review.summary: Ralph is a bash script (ralph.sh) that repeatedly launches Amp or Claude Code with a fresh context, each time picking the highest-priority story in prd.json where passes is false. It implements one story, runs typecheck and tests, commits on success, and records learnings in progress.txt and AGENTS.md. It also ships prd and ralph skills for writing a PRD and converting it to prd.json.
review.audience: Developers who want unattended coding-agent runs against a PRD task list
strengths: Fresh context each iteration; state persists only in git, progress.txt and prd.json
Supports both Amp and Claude Code via a --tool flag
Small footprint: one shell script, prompt templates and two skills, plus jq
Installable as a Claude Code plugin marketplace entry
weaknesses: Needs working typecheck and tests; broken checks compound across iterations
Stories must fit one context window; large ones must be split by hand
Requires an authenticated Amp or Claude Code install, which are separate tools
No tagged releases; default cap is 10 iterations
needs: Needs Amp CLI or Claude Code, jq, git
